cs.t:
Every consumer router-wirelessAP I've seen runs linux.
  I never see security upgrades for the kernels they use. Not one. Not ever.
  
Turris [1] has been updating their routers for years. [1]  https://www.turris.com
cs.th: Ubuntu still has not released patch for Linux 0day RCE in almost 3 weeks

cs.t: If someone is interested in open hardware running openwrt, also check out Turris.  https://www.turris.com/en/  I have been using them for years and I'm really happy. I recently bought the WiFi 6 upgrade kit for both of my turris. They "recently" released their latest version which is expensive but comes with WiFi 7 and 2.5 Gbps RJ45 and 10 Gbps SPF.

Nah, Turris routers are still consumer products. SOHO, to be precise. ;) AFAIK, none of them supports WPA Enterprise, which I'd consider necessary for enterprise-grade equipment. OTOH, they are Open Source and Open Hardware, are still pretty powerful, and are much cheaper than enterprise HW.
